entry.title: Autumn recap
entry.content:
As we’re quickly approaching the end of November, I figured it’s time for a quick recap of what I’ve been up to this autumn 🍂

  1. Of course, the most significant thing is that my husband and I bought a new flat. I really love how bright it is! Our kitchen renovation has started, with the removal of the old kitchen, and we should hopefully be moving in towards the end of December.
  2. A couple of weeks ago, I went to the Web Summit in Lisbon for work, which made me realise how much the AI experience will go downhill from here.
  3. The only other trip was a day trip to Rye, which was a very nice day out.
  4. My JNCO collection kept growing, adding no less than three new pairs of jeans. A crazy pair of Convicts, a more wearable pair of Jesters and a very sensible pair of Low Downs.
  5. In terms of blog features, I launched a guestbook (feel free to sign it!) and a minor feature for links to related posts. The biggest improvement for me was an update to my blog generator so that I can now post from my iPad, which will be handy for the three trips I’ve got coming up. Lastly, I also added a little feature to jump to a random post.
  6. I bought a camera, a Panasonic Lumix L10. I’m quite excited, but there’s still a lot to learn, so I still seem to default to my phone. My upcoming trip to Japan should be a good opportunity to get more practice.
  7. Culture-wise, there wasn’t a lot happening, but we did go to see My Neighbour Totoro, the musical.

All in all, a pretty quiet autumn. The start of winter is looking to be rather intense, though, with the move and no fewer than three countries to visit 🛫

entry.title: Finally a proper watch again
entry.content:
The G-Shock watch I bought in the Black Friday sale arrived quickly, and so far, I love it.

I’ve had several G-Shocks through the years. After being stuck with Fitbits and Apple Watch for however many years, it feels great to finally wear a proper watch again. No daily charging, no distractions and no connectivity issues (or, indeed, connectivity!).

The vibrating alarm, which was the hard requirement for it to replace my Apple Watch, seems to do its job well. The real test, though, will be to see whether it wakes me up tomorrow! 😰

entry.title: Get ready for the enshitification of AI (and everything else with it)
entry.content:
Last week, I attended the Web Summit conference in Lisbon. I might share more thoughts and impressions later, but my biggest takeaway is not from anything anyone said, but from extrapolating from what they said.

My conclusion is this:

Using AI chats to find information will never be better than it is right now. In fact, it will go downhill from here.

This is based on how many talks focused on the theme “How do you make your brand visible when people use AI instead of web browsing to find products?”

And the approach goes like this:

  1. Figure out what people are asking the AI about where you want your brand to appear.
  2. Optimise the sources the AI feeds on to surface your brand in a positive way.
  3. Measure and iterate.

So, just as SEO made web search rubbish by rewarding optimised slop over genuine content, AI optimisation will do the same for AI. But this time, they have AI to help them take the “optimisation” to the next level.

And what’s worse, while SEO more or less only required you to repeat the same phrase over and over on a page to rank highly, AI uses multiple sources to give the best response. That means that people’s (or bots’, more likely) optimisation efforts will, by necessity, include things like social media, news sites, Wikipedia, Reddit, academic papers, reviews, blogs – basically everything.

So where SEO mainly ruined the search engines themselves, and made some pages a bit more annoying to read, the blast radius of AI optimisation is so much worse.

That doesn’t make me super-optimistic about where the web will go over the next five years.

entry.title: iPhone Duo-n’t
entry.content:
I went to see the new iPhone Duo today. I have been rather sceptical about the whole thing, but I assumed that once I held it in my hand, it would create the same kind of craving every other iPhone has.

When I first picked it up, it felt as if it might. I really liked the screen’s dimensions when closed. It felt new and fresh, different from the form factor Apple have played on repeat for so long. However, when trying to use it, I realised it’s way too wide to use comfortably with one hand while standing on the tube. And then, for the main trick, when opening the phone up to reveal the folded screen, the whole thing just felt like a slightly awkward iPad mini.

So no, iPhone Duo is not for me. I don’t get what it’s for. And at that price?
